result.summary: The image shows a narrow urban street with mixed-use buildings, featuring a marked zebra crosswalk and pedestrian signals. A large outdoor dining structure on the right side creates a significant visual obstruction for the crossing and narrows the pedestrian walkway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Outdoor Dining
hazards.description: The large enclosed outdoor dining structure on the right side of the street blocks the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, adjacent to the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Daylighting at Intersection
interventions.description: Remove or set back the outdoor dining structure at least 20 feet from the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

result.summary: The image shows a one-way urban street with a marked zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic infrastructure like curb ramps and street lighting is present, parked vehicles near the intersection create sightline obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the crosswalk on the right side of the image obstruct the sightlines between approaching drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street, adjacent to the crosswalk

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra markings are beginning to wear, which may reduce their visibility to drivers during low-light or wet conditions.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve visibility for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the crossing to shorten the crossing distance and prevent illegal parking near the crosswalk.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Refresh
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility thermoplastic markings to ensure it is clearly seen by approaching traffic.

result.summary: The image depicts an urban intersection with a high-visibility zebra crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides of a one-way street. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like curb ramps and marked crossings are present, the environment lacks traffic calming measures such as curb extensions to reduce crossing distance.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway at the crossing increases pedestrian exposure time without the benefit of curb extensions or a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground zebra crosswalk spanning the width of the street.

hazards.name: Potential sight line obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles further down the street may limit visibility for pedestrians entering the roadway if parking is allowed too close to the intersection.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street beyond the immediate crossing area.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at the intersection to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on remaining crossing time.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines for all road users.
